Event Platform · CRM Guide

Using the CRM, step by step

The CRM is where the team keeps the people it may invite to TOURISE 2027, and sees where each one stands: in the CRM, added, sent, registered, confirmed. Twelve short lessons, each on the real screen: the 1 pink numbers on the picture match the steps beside it.

Names, emails and phone numbers in the screenshots are blurred on purpose. The people shown are sample data. Your menu only shows what your role allows.

What the CRM does

The CRM links invitations and registrations, one CRM ID each; requests enter once accepted. The team used to keep its invitation lists in Excel, where a sheet cannot tell whether a person has already been invited or has registered. The CRM takes the same sheet (the client’s template v4.1), keeps every column, and adds what Excel cannot: who each contact is in the system, and one journey per person, read live from the invitation and the registration. Nothing is typed twice.

In CRMKnown, not invited yet.
→
RequestedAsked for one. ✕ Rejected.
→
AddedInvitation created; then Sent.
→
RegisteredFilled in the form. ✕ Not accepted.
→
ConfirmedAttending. ✕ Declined. Then Checked in.

Where it is

Overview → CRM in the left menu, right under the dashboards. It opens on the Master dashboard. Three tabs across the top: Contacts (everyone the team may invite, speakers included), Speakers (the speakers only, with their own columns), and Settings (the lists). On Contacts, a switch between Dashboard (the numbers) and Data (the table); the Speakers tab is its table only.

Two things to know first

Every list value is the system’s. A country, a category, an industry or a title must be one of the values the system already has, spelled as the system spells it. Settings shows every value (lesson 11).
You see your own categories. Each admin sees, edits and invites only the contacts in the categories on their account, as on Guests. A Super Admin sees everyone.
Everyone is a contact. A speaker is a contact whose Category is Speaker; the Speakers tab shows the same people with their programme columns (lesson 10).

★
Start here · How people get into the CRM

Where everyone comes from

Each invitation or registration is linked to one CRM contact with one CRM ID. Requests enter only once accepted. Records are linked, never moved: the original invitation, request or guest stays where it is.

1 · Every way in leads to one contact

The CRMAdd contact or Import contacts (lessons 5 and 6).
InvitationsAn invitation made in the Invitations section: created, from a file, with Add people, from an accepted request or a dignitary’s party.
Invitation RequestsA request enters the CRM only after it is accepted and an invitation is created. Pending and rejected requests stay in Invitation Requests; they may still appear in the history of an existing contact.
RegistrationSomeone registers on a public form (with or without an invitation), is added by an admin in Guests, or comes in on the Guests import.
2

CRM → Settings, In the system: 1 when everyone was first brought in, how many were added, and the total now. 2 Check again (Super Admin) runs the same check by hand.

Automatic. After an update the system brings everyone in by itself, once. From then on each new person is added the moment they arrive, and a nightly check picks up anything missed. Settings shows when it last ran, nightly or by hand, and how many it added and linked. Nobody needs to press a button.

The Source column says where a contact first came from: Added in the CRM, From Invitations, From an invitation request, From a registration, Added in Guests, From the Guests import.

2 · One person, one CRM ID

The CRM ID (C-000123) is the one tracking number. Guests and Invitations show it as a link back to the contact (lesson 9). The system knows it is the same person by:

The linkTheir invitation, request or registration already belongs to the contact, even if they changed their email or name when registering.
The emailThe same email, in any capitalisation, or an earlier email: someone who registers through their invitation with a new email keeps the invitation’s as “Earlier email (before registering)”.
Never the mobileTwo people may share a mobile. Both stay separate, each with a “Same mobile as C-…” warning.
Never the name aloneA matching name with another email is a new contact, with a “Similar name” warning to check. Nothing is merged by itself.

3 · What their status says

Seven stages and three stops: In CRM, Requested (✕ Rejected), Added, Sent, Registered (✕ Not accepted), Confirmed (✕ Declined), Checked in. Each status also says where the person is, as a link, and how they came in (lesson 9).

Every case on one page

The CRM cases at a glance sheet (appendix) shows every way in, every status and every case, A to K, with what the CRM shows. When they register, what they typed replaces the CRM’s copy and History records it; a blank never wipes a value.

Lesson 1 · Overview → CRM

Open the CRM and read the dashboard

The Master dashboard: one page with every figure of the CRM, read from the latest records under the filters you set. Start with the header and the key numbers.

123456789
  1. 1Select CRM in the Overview group, under Dashboard, Sponsors Dashboard and Speakers Dashboard. It opens on this page.
  2. 2The three tabs: Contacts, Speakers, Settings. Only Contacts has a dashboard; Speakers opens on its table.
  3. 3Switch between Dashboard and Data. The filters travel with you, so the numbers and the rows always agree.
  4. 4Chart or Table: every card as a chart, or as its numbers with a share and a bar.
  5. 5Print report prints the page as a report, stamped with the time the numbers were read (“Data as of”).
  1. 6Export Excel: the same figures in a workbook, one sheet per panel, each stamped with the time.
  2. 7Filters work exactly as on the table (lesson 3). Select Search to apply them, Reset to clear.
  3. 8Total invitees: everyone under the filters above.
  4. 9One tile per stage, with its count and its share of the total: In CRM, Added, Sent, Registered, Confirmed, Declined, and Requested, Rejected, Not accepted and Checked in when someone is in them. A small line shows the trend where the dates are real: Sent per week, answers per day. Click a tile to filter the page to that stage; click it again to lift it.
Where the statuses come from

The dashboard reads each person’s status from the real request, invitation, registration and answer (the Status column, lesson 9), not from what is typed on the contact. A guest invited outside the system, with a Sent Date typed by hand, is not counted as Sent: only an invitation that really went out is. Confirmed needs a Yes and an accepted registration; a Yes while the registration is still Pending counts as Registered.

Lesson 4, continued · Activity Log

Attach files to an activity

Keep the call, email or meeting and its supporting files on the contact.

  1. Open the contact and choose Log activity.
  2. Complete the date, activity type, outcome, notes and next reminder as needed.
  3. Add files before saving. You can choose several and remove a chosen file before saving.
  4. Save the activity. Each attachment appears under the entry as a link; open it there.
LimitsUp to 5 files per activity, each up to 5 MB.
Accepted typesPDF, JPG/JPEG, PNG, WebP, XLSX and DOCX.
Private filesFiles stay private and open through signed links. Reopen the contact to get a fresh link if one expires.
Delete an activityDeleting the activity also removes its attachments.

5
Lesson 5, continued · Category = Speaker

A speaker on the Contacts form

Choose Speaker as the Category and the contact becomes a speaker when saved. The form then asks what a speaker needs, and the red stars change with it.

123456

With 2 Category = Speaker, 1 Sector, 3 Sub-category, 4 Tier and 5 Source List lose their star; 6 Relationship Owner keeps it.

1234

1 Channel and 2 Clearance are optional for a speaker; 3 Invitation Sent By and 4 Follow up are required.

Required for a speaker

Category, First and Last Name, Job Title, Company, Email, Gender, Country of Residence, Relationship Owner, Invitation Sent By, Follow up and Notes.

Optional for a speaker

Tier, Sector, Industry, Sub-category, Seniority, Channel, Clearance, Source List, List Provided By and the rest. A speaker has no channel or clearance check when invited.

Changing the Category

To Speaker: the contact becomes a speaker and appears on the Speakers tab. Its speaker-only fields (Day, Pillar, Session, Bio, Keyword…) start empty; fill them there.
Away from Speaker: the person is a plain contact again and its speaker details are removed. History records what they held.

What the form refuses

A Category that is not one of your own. H.E.’s Office with clearance Not Required (for a contact). A Sub-category that is not under the Category chosen. A status other than the team’s three.

5
Lesson 5, continued · Add contact

Already in the system?

Before a contact is saved, the form checks the email against the CRM and the rest of the system, so nobody is added twice.

12
  1. 1Type the email. The form looks for this person as you leave the field.
  2. 2“Already in the system: registered … invited … requested …”, each with a link. Saving links the new contact to those records instead of making a second person. “Already in the CRM as C-…” means they have a contact: open it instead.
Registration data is kept

When the person has registered, the form says so: on saving, their name, email, phone and the other shared details come from the registration, not from what is typed. The guest’s details always win; change them on the guest.

Relationship Owner

Picked from the admins with CRM access. For an admin set to “Only contacts they own” (lesson 12), a new contact is theirs by default.

Lesson 6 · CRM → Import contacts

Import contacts from Excel

Choose Add new contacts or Update contacts. Check the file first: valid rows can be imported while rows with problems are kept for download. A whole-file problem or no valid rows stops the import.

123456
  1. 1Before you upload: the rules a file follows, in short.
  2. 2Choose file: Excel or CSV, up to 5,000 rows. The Contacts sheet is read if there is one; the client’s example row is skipped.
  3. 3Download Excel sample: first opens a summary of required and optional columns, then downloads the template with working dropdowns from the system’s lists.
  1. 4Check the file reads every row and lists each problem (next page).
  2. 5Import opens after checking when at least one row is valid and the file has no whole-file problem. The summary says how many rows will be kept out.
  3. 6Past imports: each file, when, by whom, how many added, updated and not imported. Download the failed rows to fix them. Contacts opens the imported contacts.

What a file needs

RuleWhat it means
HeadingsThe template’s, or the client’s (Prefix, Mobile, Follow-up sent … are read). Columns are matched by heading; any match can be changed before checking.
Required columnsFor Add new contacts: Prefix, First Name, Last Name, Email, Category, Sub-category when the category has one, Tier when you may see it, Source List (File Name), List Provided By, and History / Source. Other columns are optional. Use the current sample, not an older required-fields list.
List valuesWritten as the system’s list has them; only case and extra spaces are forgiven. “Saudi” is not “Saudi Arabia”. Settings shows every value (lesson 11).
CRM IDUpdate contacts requires a CRM ID on every row and updates only that contact. Add new contacts does not update people matched by email; an existing email is reported with the CRM ID and who added it. Use Update contacts for existing contacts.
Never importedPassport and ID numbers, dates of birth, photos: a file with such a column is refused outright.
Sent Date, Sent ByRead as written (invited outside the system). A file’s Invitation Status is last year’s record, kept with the row only.
Owner, Follow upRelationship Owner: an admin of the system, by name or email; otherwise “… is not an admin in the system”. Follow up: Yes or No; Y/N, true/false, 1/0, نعم / لا are read too. Both are dropdowns in the template.
SpeakersImport on the Speakers tab with the speakers’ own columns. Category Speaker in a contacts import is refused; a contacts update cannot convert a contact to Speaker.

A clean file goes in

After checking, the summary shows valid rows, changes and rows with problems. Import processes valid rows; a clean file imports all rows.

1 “No problems. Importing adds 5 contacts and updates 0.” 2 Import creates and updates them in one go.

  2. 2Select Import. A message confirms the counts, the form clears, and the file appears under Past imports.

The same person twice

The same email or CRM ID twice in one file: both rows are refused, naming each other’s row. A shared mobile is a warning, not a reason to merge people. The same first and last name with another email is imported and flagged as a possible duplicate for the team to look at; nothing is ever merged by itself.

Lesson 6, continued · CRM → Import contacts

Who the file matches

The check says, row by row, who is already in the CRM and what importing will change.

After Check the file: “Already in the CRM: C-… · invited … · registered … as …”, the contact each row updates, and which fields stay as the registration has them.

Matched by emailCurrent or earlier email, any capitalisation. In Add new contacts, an existing email is refused and the message says who added the contact (an admin or the system). Update contacts identifies the contact by CRM ID; the registration’s protected fields stay as registered. The Speakers import can match existing speakers by email.
Fields that changeListed with readable column names; those kept from the registration are named too.
Same name onlyA new contact, with “Similar name: C-…” to check.
Same mobileA new contact, with “Same mobile as C-…”. A mobile never links two rows.
Rows kept outInvalid values, missing required fields, duplicate email or CRM ID, a contact outside your access, or a speaker in a contacts file. A whole-file problem such as a forbidden personal-data column stops all rows.
Test files

tourise-docs/client/CRM_IMPORT_TEST_CASES/ holds two files built from the template: TEST_1_valid (10 rows that should all import) and TEST_2_errors (6 rows, each with its own problem; none can be imported until a row is fixed). Each has a Test cases sheet saying what every row should do, with a Result column to fill in. They change real contacts: use them on a local or test system only.

Lesson 6, continued · Update contacts

Update from an exported file

Change existing contacts using the same file the Contacts table exports.

  1. Filter or select the contacts on Contacts → Data, then Export.
  2. Edit the cells in Excel. Keep the CRM ID on every row: it identifies the contact, even if its email changes.
  3. Open Import contacts → Update contacts, choose the file, map the columns and Check the file.
  4. Review the changes, then import valid rows. Download the rows kept out to correct and check again.
Empty cellsLeave the existing value unchanged. To clear a field, use Edit.
What cannot changeSystem status and Region are calculated; registration-owned fields stay as the guest gave them. Speaker rows use Import speakers.
Rows kept outMissing or unknown CRM ID, a contact outside your access, a speaker, duplicate identifiers, or invalid field values. New people belong in Add new contacts.
AccessThe role needs Update import. Add new contacts uses Create. Each mode has its own past-import list.
Check again after editing the preview

Changing a cell, mapping or row invalidates the previous check. Check again before importing. Download the edited file to keep the corrections you made on screen.

What can be changed in bulk

The team’s fieldsInvitation Status (Not Sent, In Progress, Pending) · Invitation Channel · Security Clearance · Relationship Owner (an admin) · Follow up (Yes, No) · Invitation Sent Date · Invitation Sent By
Any listTitle, Company Location, Gender, Nationality, Country, Sector, Industry, Seniority, Category, Tier, Source List and History / Source. List Provided By is entered as text. A Category asks for its Sub-category, an Industry for its Sub-industry.
The rulesEach contact is checked as if edited alone. Those that pass are saved; the rest are listed with the reason. Ticked speakers are changed too (with the speakers’ Update box). Fields kept from a registration are left as registered, and listed.
Who did it

Every bulk change is written to each contact’s History and to the Audit trail, with the admin’s name.

Lesson 7, continued · Archived

Archive, restore or delete permanently

Remove a contact from the active CRM while keeping its data, history and links.

ArchiveUse Archive on the contact window or select rows and Archive on the table. Confirm. The contact leaves the active list.
Open ArchivedSelect Archived above the table. Contacts and Speakers have their own archive pages, with Archived on and Archived by columns.
RestoreSelect the archived contacts and restore them to the active list. View archived grants access and restore.
Delete permanentlyAvailable only in Archived, with its separate permission and confirmation. It removes the CRM contact for good; linked invitations and registrations stay in their own sections.
Actions on one contact

The contact window now offers Invite and Archive at the top when your role allows them; no table selection is needed.

8
Lesson 8 · Tick contacts → Invite

Invite contacts

Invite the ticked contacts into their category’s CRM collection. The collection decides the email, the sub-category, the tier and the link settings; the CRM only says who.

12345

Create targeted collection, once per category: 1 category, 2 sub-category, 3 email template, account and tier, 4 usage, then 5 Create. It appears on Invitations as “CRM - Category”.

1234

1 The collection; 2 what every invitation will carry; 3 Add only or 4 Add and send.

  1. 1Tick the contacts, select Invite, and pick the Targeted collection of their category; a missing one can be created from the link.
  2. 2Under the field: the email template, the sub-category and the tier every invitation will carry.
  1. 3Add only creates the invitations without sending. The Status column and journey read Added; the team’s Invitation Status is In Progress. Send later from Invitations.
  2. 4Add and send makes and sends them now. The journey reads Added until the email goes out, then Sent; the team’s Invitation Status starts at In Progress.
1

After Add only or Add and send: the contacts the rules stopped, each with its reason. The others have an invitation created: Added in tracking, In Progress in the team’s Invitation Status, then Sent once sent. Ticked speakers are invited too (no channel or clearance check), with the speakers’ Invite box.

Who is skipped, and why

Channel is not CRM“Invited through H.E.’s Office, not from the system.” That invitation goes out through the office. The same for MOFA, Royal Court, Other Ministries and Relationship Owner.
Clearance not Approved or Not Required“Security clearance pending”, “not submitted”, or “not approved: escalate to Fahad”.
Already invited, sent or registeredNobody is invited twice, even when the first invitation was made on Invitations.
No addressAn email collection needs an email; SMS or WhatsApp needs a mobile. A pending request does not block inviting from the CRM; it stays in Invitation Requests and is not automatically accepted.
9
Lesson 9 · The Status column, and the window

Follow where each contact is

For every contact the system reads the real request, invitation and registration, and shows the furthest step reached. Nothing here is typed, except the team’s note on In CRM.

StageReached whenShown with
In CRMKnown, not invited yet.The team’s note: Not Sent, In Progress, Pending
Requested ✕ RejectedThey asked for an invitation; Rejected when the request was turned down.The request’s status; link to it
AddedAn invitation has been created but has not been sent. Add only reaches this stage; it does not contact the person.The collection
SentThe invitation went out.Delivered, Opened, or ↳ Not delivered
Registered ✕ Not acceptedThey filled in the form; Not accepted when the team rejected or cancelled it.The registration’s status: Pending, On-hold, Accepted
Confirmed ✕ DeclinedRegistration accepted and they said they are attending; Declined when they said no. A Yes while still Pending reads “Registered (Pending) · attending: yes”.Date
Checked inScanned at the gate.Date and time

Where they are, and how they came in

Every status says where the person is, as a link that opens it: in Invitation Requests · in Invitations (the collection) · in Guests (the category) · only in the CRM. Under it, smaller, how they came in: via CRM · via Invitations · via Request · Registered by themselves · via Guests import · added in Guests.

For example: Sent · in Invitations (VIP 2027), via CRM; Requested (Pending) · in Invitation Requests, via Request; Registered (Accepted) · in Guests (Media), Registered by themselves.

1

On Guests and on Invitations, a 1 CRM C-000020 chip shows which contact the person came from and opens it in the CRM.

Filters made for follow-up

Status finds every contact at a stage. Sent, not opened (3+, 7+, 14+ or 30+ days) lists the invitations to chase. Sent, not registered lists those who opened but never registered. Needs follow-up lists those the next page describes.

9
Lesson 9, continued · Follow-ups

Who needs following up

The system tells each Relationship Owner who needs a call, by a bell in the table and a daily alert.

WhyReminder overdue: the Next Reminder Date has passed. No follow-up after the invitation: sent N days ago or more (7 by default), Follow up still empty, nothing in the Activity Log since, and no answer yet.
The bellAn amber bell beside the name, in the table and in the window’s header. Hover it for the reason and the days overdue; click it to Log activity.
The badge and filter“🔔 N need follow-up” above the table filters to them; the Needs follow-up filter does the same, by reason. Combine it with Relationship Owner to see one owner’s list.
AlertsEvery day at 08:00 (Riyadh time) the owner gets a bell 🔔 alert in the header for each contact that needs following up, once per reason. They are also alerted when they are made a contact’s Relationship Owner, once with the count for a bulk change or an import.
Only ownersOnly a contact with a Relationship Owner (an admin) needs following up: the owner is who is told.
123

CRM → Settings, Follow-ups (the Settings box): 1 how many days after the invitation, 2 the daily check time, 3 which alerts the owner gets. Save applies them.

The Speakers tab

Everyone is a contact: a speaker is a contact whose Category is Speaker. The Speakers tab shows the speakers alone, with the programme’s columns, to list, add, edit and import them. It has no dashboard.

123456
  1. 1Add speaker: the form in the speakers’ groups: Session, Speaker, Invitation, Contact person, Profile.
  2. 2Import speakers: the team’s Speaker Required Fields sheet. This is where speakers are imported with their own columns.
  3. 3The tab opens straight on its table: no Dashboard switch.
  1. 4The speaker-only columns, here Day and Session: Day, Pillar, Session, Keyword, Type, Option #, Continent, Bio, Social Handles and the rest show on this tab only.
  2. 5Status works as for contacts: the team’s status until invited, then the journey.
  3. 6Follow up: Yes or No.

How speakers differ

The speakers’ formOn this tab, every column of the speakers’ sheet is required for now, on the form and in a speakers’ file.
The speakers’ listsDay, Pillar, Session (the programme’s 57), Type, Continent, and Official invite to be sent by (a title); read-only in Settings.
No channel, no clearanceInviting skips only those already invited, sent, registered, or without an email. Speakers go into the Speaker category’s collection (“CRM - Speaker”).
One email, one recordAn email is on one person only, speaker or not.
Its own windowA speaker opens in the speaker’s window from either tab (Session, Speaker, and Invitation with Sent Date, Sent By, Follow up); Edit opens the speaker’s form.

Speakers on the Contacts tab

Find themFilter Category = Speaker. There is no Type column; the speaker-only columns (Day, Pillar, Session, Bio, Keyword…) show on the Speakers tab only.

Lesson 11 · CRM → Settings

Settings: the lists

Settings opens with two boxes: In the system (the read-only sync status, page “Where everyone comes from”) and Follow-ups (lesson 9). Below them, the lists. Source List (File Name) is the team’s editable list. List Provided By is now typed freely on the contact or in the file. Every other list is the system’s, shown here so a file can be written to match it.

123456
  1. 1The Settings tab. A red star marks the lists every contact needs a value from.
  2. 2Source List (File Name): the team’s list. Add a value here before importing a file that uses it. List Provided By needs no Settings value.
  3. 3Type the new value and Add value. A value is never renamed or deleted.
  1. 4Untick Active to switch a value off once no contact holds it (move them in bulk first, lesson 7). It stays on old records and is no longer offered.
  2. 5The count opens the contacts holding that value.
  3. 6The system lists, read-only: Title, Company Location, Gender, Nationality, Country, Sector, Industry, Sub-industry, Seniority, Category, Sub-category, Tier, History / Source. They are kept in Titles, Countries, Categories and the registration forms.
12

A system list, read-only: the English and Arabic name of every value, and for Sub-category and Sub-industry the parent each sits under. 2 Search a long list.

Why the exact spelling matters

A file is matched to these lists exactly as written here, forgiving only case and extra spaces. Whoever cleans a client’s file can open the list, search it, and copy each value as it is.

Sub-categories

A Super Admin enters them in Management → Categories, on each category. A category with no list asks for no sub-category.

Lesson 12 · Management → Roles

Who can do what

The CRM is switched on per role, box by box. Each admin then works within the categories on their own account.

The CRM card in the role editor: the contacts’ boxes, Invite, the speakers’ own boxes and the shared ones. The hint at the top says who sees which contacts.

BoxWhat it opens
ViewThe Contacts tab and its table, the window, search and filters, the CRM chip on Guests and Invitations.
View dashboardThe Contacts dashboard. Without it the tab opens on the table.
CreateAdd contact, Import contacts, Download Excel sample.
UpdateEdit, the pencil in the window and in the cells, Edit selected, the photo. A speaker’s row on Contacts also needs Edit speakers.
ArchiveArchive one contact or the ticked contacts, keeping their data and links.
View archived / Delete permanentlySeparate boxes: View archived opens the archive and allows restore; Delete permanently removes archived contacts for good.
Update contacts by importIts own box, Update import, opens the Update contacts mode; Create opens Add new contacts.
InviteCreate targeted collection, and Invite.
View speakers … Invite speakersThe same for the Speakers tab: view, add and import, edit, archive, restore and delete permanently, invite (with the corresponding boxes). View speakers also lists the speakers on Contacts. View speakers dashboard is still in the list but opens nothing: there is no speakers dashboard.
SettingsThe Settings tab: adding and switching off the team’s list values.
Record HistoryThe History button on a contact’s window.
Audit TrailThe Audit trail button: every CRM action, with export.
1

Tier is not a CRM box: 1 View tier (guests, invitations, CRM), under Guests, shows and hides Tier everywhere at once.

Categories, not roles, draw the line

What an admin may do comes from the role. Which contacts they see comes from the categories on their admin account (Management → Admins), the same scope that limits Guests and Invitations. An admin limited to Sponsor sees, imports, edits and invites Sponsor contacts only; a file with a Dignitary row is refused for them. A Super Admin sees all.

Without View tier the Tier column, filter, chart and field are simply not there, and an import ignores a Tier column.

Lesson 12, continued · Management → Admins

Which contacts each admin sees

Besides the role, two things on an admin decide which contacts they see: their categories, and their CRM data setting.

12

On each admin’s page, CRM data: 1 All contacts or 2 Only contacts they own.

All contactsEvery contact in their categories.
Only their ownOnly the contacts where they are the Relationship Owner, within their categories. They get alerts only for those, and a contact they add is theirs by default.
RequestsContacts from an invitation request with no matching category are shown to admins whose role can view Invitation Requests (with the CRM View box).
Super AdminAlways sees every contact.
Relationship Owner is an admin account

The owner is picked from the admins with CRM access, so a renamed admin is renamed on their contacts too. A file may name them by name or email. An old owner typed as text reads “Was: … (not an admin account). Pick an admin.” until it is changed.

Reference

Rules at a glance

Channel, clearance and speakers

RuleWhat the system does
CRM or an empty channel sendsA contact on any other channel (H.E.’s Office, MOFA, Royal Court, Other Ministries, Relationship Owner) is never invited from the CRM: that invitation goes out through the office. The team follows it with In Progress, Pending and the notes.
H.E.’s Office needs a clearanceNot Required cannot be chosen with that channel, on the form, in a cell, in bulk or in a file.
Clearance gates sendingAn empty Security Clearance does not block inviting. When filled, only Approved or Not Required allow it; Not Submitted and Pending wait, and Not Approved says “escalate to Fahad”.
One person, one CRM IDMatched by the link or email (current or earlier), never by mobile or name alone. The guest’s details win.
A speaker is a contactCategory = Speaker makes a speaker; its row also needs the speakers’ boxes.
Checked in bulk tooInviting 200 with 30 stopped invites 170 and lists the 30 with a reason each; a bulk edit works the same way.

The two statuses, side by side

StatusWho sets itWhen
Not SentThe teamEvery new contact starts here.
In ProgressThe team, or the systemBeing worked on; set by the system when an invitation is made (Add only).
PendingThe teamWaiting on something: a clearance, an office, an answer.
RequestedThe systemFrom the invitation request.
SentThe systemThe invitation was sent. Sent Date and Sent By are filled only if empty; a value typed by hand stays.
Accepted · DeclinedThe systemFrom the invitation and the guest’s answer. Shown in the Status column as Registered, Confirmed or Declined.

What is never done by itself

No sending on importA file only fills the CRM. Invitations are made and sent in lesson 8, by someone.
No sending on a status changeSetting a status, alone or in bulk, sends nothing.
No guessing, no mergingA value that does not match its list keeps that row out; other valid rows can import. A possible duplicate by name or mobile is flagged, never merged.
Quick help

When something doesn’t work

ProblemWhat to doLesson
The CRM is not in my menuIt is in Overview, under the dashboards. If it is not there, your role has no CRM box: ask a Super Admin to tick View (and the rest you need).1, 12
The dashboard’s Sent differs from the contact’s statusIt reads the real invitation: a Sent Date typed by hand does not count as Sent there.1, 9
I see fewer contacts than my colleagueYou see your categories only, and only your own contacts if your CRM data is “Only contacts they own”. Ask a Super Admin.12
The file “can’t be imported yet”Read the problems. Correct red cells in the preview and check again, or download the failed rows and fix them in Excel. Import valid rows when offered. Whole-file problems must be fixed first.6, 11
“Not on the Source List list”Add the value in Settings first, then check the file again.11
“This email is already on CRM contact C-000…”The person is in the CRM already. Use Export and Update contacts with that CRM ID, or edit the contact. Add new contacts does not update an existing email.6
The file has a passport or ID columnRemove the column and choose the file again. Such data is never imported.6
A mobile is refusedWrite it with + and the country code: +966501234567.6
Invite is greyTick at least one contact first. If the button is missing, your role has no Invite box.8, 12
“No targeted collections” in the Invite dialogCreate the category’s collection from the link in the dialog, or with Create targeted collection.8
A contact was “not invited”Read its reason: the channel sends elsewhere, a filled clearance is not Approved or Not Required, or the person already has an invitation or registration.8
“… is not an admin in the system”The owner must be an admin, by name or email. Pick from the list or the template’s dropdown.5, 6
Where are the speakers, and their dashboard?On Contacts and on its dashboard, filter Category = Speaker (shown with the speakers’ View box). There is no speakers dashboard and no Type column any more.1, 10
I can’t edit a speaker’s cell on ContactsIt needs Edit speakers as well as Update. In bulk, such rows come back as failed with the reason.7, 12
A file “Write Yes or No”Follow up takes Yes or No (also Y/N, true/false, 1/0, نعم / لا). Use the template’s dropdown.6
I cannot set the status to Sent or AcceptedThose come from the invitation. The team sets Not Sent, In Progress and Pending only.9
A field says “from the registration” and can’t be editedThe person registered: change it on the guest.4
“Same mobile as C-…” or “Similar name”Two contacts look alike. Check them: nothing is merged by itself.·, 6
I get no follow-up alertsOnly the Relationship Owner (an admin) is told, and only for the alerts switched on in Settings.9
Tier is nowhere to be seenYour role lacks View tier (under Guests in Roles).12
No Sub-category can be chosenThe category has no list yet. A Super Admin adds sub-categories under Management → Categories.11
A Source List value cannot be switched offContacts still hold it. Move them to another value in bulk, then switch it off.7, 11
Appendix · Updated 29 October 2026

CRM cases at a glance

CaseCurrent behaviour
In the CRM onlyThe person can register on an available public form or request an invitation. CRM membership alone never means already registered.
Invitation created, not sentTracking reads Added. No email was sent. A public registration or invitation request is still allowed if there is no earlier registration or request.
Invitation sentTracking reads Sent, with delivery and opening details. Registration changes it to Registered.
Already registeredThe public email check reports already registered. A new registration is not created with that same email.
Already requestedThe request form reports already requested. Pending and rejected requests do not enter the CRM by themselves; acceptance creates an invitation and links the contact.
Registers before our invitationThe registration links to the existing contact by email, keeps the CRM ID, and updates the registration fields. The person is not invited again from the CRM.
Add new contacts finds an existing emailThe row is kept out. The message names the contact and who added it. Export and use Update contacts to change it.
A file has good and bad rowsImport the good rows and download the bad ones with their reasons. A whole-file problem or no good rows prevents importing.
ArchiveThe contact leaves the active list and keeps its history and links. Restore from Archived; Delete permanently is a separate permission and confirmation.

Invitations, collections and sending are covered in the Admin Panel Tutorial. This table replaces the older screenshot of the cases sheet.

Can someone in CRM register before being invited?

Yes. A CRM contact alone, or an invitation created but not sent, does not trigger an “email already exists” message on the public forms. Registration checks existing Guests; Request an invitation checks existing Guests and previous requests. After registration, the system links the guest to the same CRM contact by email and updates its journey. No invitation is sent by this link.
